steps.prompt: Two facts: “The power went out.” “We finished the game by flashlight.” Join them in a way that shows WHEN or WHY something happened. Which word did you use to join them?

cards.title: One main idea, one helper
cards.body: A complex sentence has one independent clause and at least one dependent clause. The dependent clause can’t stand alone: it starts with a word like because, when, although, if, since, until, while, or who, which, that.

cards.title: Dependent clause first or last
cards.text:
First (add a comma): Although it rained, we finished the game.
Last (usually no comma): We finished the game although it rained.
In the middle: The girl who won the race is my cousin.
cards.note: Moving the dependent clause changes the emphasis: the end of a sentence is where readers notice most.

cards.title: Why essays love complex sentences
cards.body: They show how ideas connect: cause (because), contrast (although), condition (if), time (when, after). “Schools should start later because teenagers need more sleep” is a claim and a reason in one sentence.

prompts: Which subordinating conjunction will you use most in essays? Why?
Did putting the dependent clause first or last change how your sentence sounds?
